browser_proof.scope: Root actually viewed all 11 frozen v3 screenshots and the three licensed source photographs. Catalog lifecycle is a separate pending check.

roof.scope: Targeted actual triangle proof and root native review support separated main tile courses and corrected sign/eave placement. Inferred side gables close the envelope; hidden roof depth, ridge and rear geometry are estimates.

size_proof.scope: All four actual packaged assets are byte/SHA verified and each is strictly below100000000bytes. Published triangle/bounds figures come from the bound actual package/decoder reports. LOD remains a geometric simplification, not a pixel-identical appearance proof.

source_photos.scope: Original Fayhoo CC BY-SA3 JPEG bytes and source metadata verified; source photo was actually viewed by root with the v3 native preview and independently for navigation. Commons2013 versus EXIF2016 conflict remains explicit. No photograph is embedded in raw/web/LOD.

texture_mapping_qa.scope: Intentional no-photo-texture architecture. Actual package and production decoder reports have0embedded images for raw/web/LOD; original source JPEGs remain downloadable geometry references. Materials are inferred, not calibrated reflectance.

uncertainty.scope: Original documented geometry/source estimates remain. Subsequent actual v3 static HTML and root visual acceptance are bound separately below; the new two-macro catalog lifecycle still awaits its own test. This is two additional individually modeled buildings and integration of the previously published Wukang 129; not citywide photographic reconstruction. Hidden rear elevations, heights and some materials remain inferred from licensed photos and available footprints. Surrounding streets, vegetation and generic neighboring buildings are not newly reconstructed by this batch. Distant LOD captures are small and partly occluded; they verify switching with decoded-asset checks but do not independently certify facade detail. The reviewed tea-house close oblique view crops the left edge and base; the front and return views cover these areas. Software rendering is not a hardware performance or frame-rate acceptance test. Reviewed fixed camera poses and lifecycle states do not establish collision-free walking from every possible angle.
